stated: The Conservative Party pledges to abolish the main rate of self-employed National Insurance entirely by the end of the next Parliament, building on the abolition of Class 2 contributions from April this year.

source.quote: For the very smallest businesses, the four million people who are self-employed, we will abolish the main rate of National Insurance entirely by the end of the next Parliament. … This is a massive simplification of the tax system which means that 93% of self-employed people – four million of them – will no longer pay self-employed National Insurance. This will not affect their entitlement to the State Pension.

bearing_set.reason: Abolishing Class 4 NI directly raises the net earnings of ~4-5 million self-employed workers, materially affecting whether self-employment delivers a decent, secure living.
For self-employed households — including lower-income ones — the reduction in NI liability increases real disposable income, bearing directly on the ability to afford essentials.
Abolishing Class 4 self-employed NI is a direct reduction in the tax burden on roughly 4 million self-employed workers, materially raising their take-home pay — the core O11 indicator.

Class 4 NI raises several billion pounds annually; full abolition creates a significant revenue gap that, unless explicitly offset, widens the funded/borrowed balance — a concrete O12 mechanism with a specific fiscal indicator.

membership_note: Primary bearing is O11 (direct take-home pay gain for self-employed). O12 is the symmetric cost-home for this unfunded tax cut. O13 (entrepreneurship stimulus) is a plausible but weak and speculative secondary effect that does not clear the non-negligible bar independently; O14 distributional effects are ambiguous given the wide income spread of the self-employed.
